claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys have limited strength and ductility in their initial state.
Phase-selective recrystallization will simultaneously increase the strength and ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Phase-selective recrystallization will refine the grain structure.
Phase-selective recrystallization will optimize the phase distribution.
The refined grain structure will enhance grain-boundary strengthening.
The resulting microstructure will improve dislocation mobility.
Enhanced grain-boundary strengthening and improved dislocation mobility will produce simultaneous gains in strength and ductility.
The strength and ductility gains will occur relative to as-cast or conventionally processed eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The effect is intended to hold across various eutectic high-entropy-alloy compositions and microstructures used in structural applications.
The magnitude of the effect depends on alloy composition, microstructure, and processing conditions.
Failure to obtain a significant increase in both strength and ductility relative to the conventional baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
